S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor_event: Taking on a mortgage (for home, business)
patient_info.stressor: When Samuel took on a business mortgage to lease and outfit a small workshop for his planned renewable-energy contracting firm, the financial stakes made his usual meticulousness around electrical safety feel newly consequential. Over time, intrusive doubts about whether he had missed a code issue or left something dangerous behind began following him from job sites into evenings that had once been reserved for karaoke, softball, and barbecue with friends. He responded by repeating checks and mental reviews far beyond normal trade practice, slowing bids, irritating apprentices, and making it difficult to keep the new venture on schedule. After a longtime contractor-client questioned why a simple smart-home installation had taken several extra visits, Samuel used his employee assistance benefits to request a psychiatric evaluation.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: Even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought keeps barging in on me that maybe I missed one loose neutral or left something that could start a fire, and I try to shake it off but it follows me all the way home.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: What brings me in is I keep going back over jobs again and again—checking breakers, labels, torque marks, photos, even driving back to a site sometimes—until a simple install takes way longer than it should and people are starting to notice.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My business schedule is slipping because jobs I should finish in one visit turn into callbacks and extra checks, and it is starting to cost me client confidence and time with the apprentices. I have also been skipping things I used to enjoy after work because I am still tied up reviewing a job or worrying about whether I need to go back.
